{{Lowercase title}}
'''mcrypt''' is a replacement for the popular [[Unix]] [[Crypt (Unix)|crypt]] command. crypt was a file encryption tool that used an [[algorithm]] very close to the [[World War&nbsp;II]] [[Enigma machine|Enigma]] cipher. Mcrypt provides the same functionality but uses several modern algorithms such as [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]]. Libmcrypt, Mcrypt's companion, is a library of code that contains the actual encryption functions and provides an easy method for use. The last update to libmcrypt was in 2007,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/mcrypt/files/Libmcrypt/ |title=Libmcrypt releases}}</ref> despite years of unmerged patches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sourceforge.net/p/mcrypt/patches |title=Libmcrypt patches}}</ref> Maintained alternatives include [[ccrypt]], [[libressl]], and others.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://paragonie.com/blog/2015/05/if-you-re-typing-word-mcrypt-into-your-code-you-re-doing-it-wrong |title=If You're Typing the Word MCRYPT Into Your PHP Code, You're Doing It Wrong |author=Paragon Initiative Enterprises}}</ref>

Examples of mcrypt usage in a Linux command-line environment:
<syntaxhighlight lang=bash>
 mcrypt --list                           # See available encryption algorithms.           
 mcrypt -a blowfish myfilename           # Encrypts myfilename to myfilename.nc           
                                         # using the Blowfish encryption algorithm.       
                                         # You are prompted two times for a passphrase.   
 mcrypt -d mytextfile.txt.nc             # Decrypts mytextfile.txt.nc to mytextfile.txt.  
 mcrypt -V -d -a enigma -o scrypt --bare # Can en/decrypt files crypted with SunOS crypt. 
 mcrypt --help
</syntaxhighlight>

It implements numerous [[cryptography|cryptographic]] algorithms, mostly [[block cipher]]s and [[stream cipher]]s, some of which fall under [[export of cryptography|export restrictions]] in the [[United States]]. Algorithms include [[Data Encryption Standard|DES]], [[blowfish (cipher)|Blowfish]], [[RC4|ARCFOUR]], Enigma, [[GOST (block cipher)|GOST]], [[LOKI97]], [[RC2]], [[Serpent (cipher)|Serpent]], [[3-Way]], [[Twofish]], [[WAKE (cipher)|WAKE]], and [[XTEA]].
